crepe_hop_length.tooltip: Only used by Crepe and Mangio-Crepe methods. Lower values track pitch changes more closely but cost more time and memory.

filter_radius.tooltip: Only meaningful for Harvest smoothing in this backend. 0 means no extra smoothing; higher values smooth more but can flatten detail.

f0_autotune.tooltip: Snap the extracted pitch contour toward the nearest musical note after pitch detection. Can help singing or stylized output, but often sounds artificial on normal speech.

use_cache.tooltip: Reuse cached loaded RVC/HuBERT models where possible for repeated processing. Usually worth leaving on.

batch_size.tooltip: Crepe-family pitch batch size hint. Higher can be faster but uses more memory. Ignored by non-Crepe methods.

use_cache.tooltip:
🚀 CACHING SYSTEM

Enables intelligent caching of separation results for faster processing:

• ❌ OFF: Always processes from scratch, uses more time but ensures fresh results

aggressiveness.tooltip:
🎚️ SEPARATION AGGRESSIVENESS (0-20)

Controls separation strength for VR architecture models (HP5, DeNoise, DeEcho, etc.):

📊 RECOMMENDED VALUES:
• 0-5: Gentle separation, preserves more original audio quality
• 6-10: ⭐ BALANCED (Default: 10) - Good separation with minimal artifacts
• 11-15: Aggressive separation, may introduce artifacts but better isolation
• 16-20: Maximum aggression, highest separation but potential quality loss

🎯 USE CASES:
• 🎤 Karaoke Creation: 12-15 (more aggressive)
• 🎵 Vocal Extraction: 8-12 (balanced)
• 🎼 Preserve Music Quality: 5-8 (gentle)
• 🔧 Problem Audio: 15-20 (maximum effort)

⚠️ NOTE: Only affects VR Architecture models (HP5, DeNoise, DeEcho). Advanced models (UVR-MDX-NET, bs_roformer, MDX23C) ignore this setting.
💡 Higher values = stronger vocal/instrumental separation but may affect audio quality

format.tooltip:
🎵 OUTPUT AUDIO FORMAT

Selects the audio format for separated stems:

🏆 QUALITY RANKING:
• 📀 FLAC: ⭐ BEST - Lossless compression, perfect quality, larger files
• 🎵 WAV: Uncompressed, perfect quality, largest files  
• 🎧 MP3: Lossy compression, smaller files, slight quality loss

💼 PROFESSIONAL USE: FLAC (default)
🚀 FAST WORKFLOW: MP3 (smaller files, faster I/O)

📊 FILE SIZE COMPARISON (typical 4-minute song):

audio1.tooltip: Primary audio input. Accepts AUDIO format.

audio2.tooltip: Secondary audio input. Accepts AUDIO format.

merge_algorithm.tooltip:
🎚️ AUDIO MERGING ALGORITHMS

Choose how to combine multiple audio sources:

📊 MATHEMATICAL ALGORITHMS:
• MEAN: ⭐ Average all inputs - smooth, balanced mix (recommended)
• MEDIAN: Reduces outliers and noise - cleaner output, less distortion
• MAX: Takes loudest signal at each point - preserves peaks, can be harsh
• MIN: Takes quietest signal at each point - gentle, subdued mix
• SUM: Simple addition - louder but may clip without normalization

🎵 CREATIVE ALGORITHMS:
• OVERLAY: Professional layering with gain compensation - natural mixing
• WEIGHTED: Custom balance using volume_balance slider - precise control
• CROSSFADE: Smooth transitions between sources - cinematic blending

💡 USE CASES:
🎤 Voice + Music: MEAN or OVERLAY
🎼 Multiple instruments: MEDIAN (reduces conflicts)
🔊 Emphasize loudest: MAX
🎛️ Custom balance: WEIGHTED
🎬 Smooth transitions: CROSSFADE
🔧 Precise control: SUM + normalization

restoration_mode.tooltip:
🤐 VOICE FIXER RESTORATION MODES

MODE 0 - ORIGINAL (Recommended for most audio):
• Removes noise, reverberation, clipping artifacts
• Balanced approach for general degraded speech
• Works well with speech that has some background noise
• Best for: Podcasts, recordings, voice calls

MODE 1 - WITH HIGH-FREQUENCY REMOVAL:
• Original restoration + aggressive high-frequency filtering
• Removes harsh sibilants and high-frequency artifacts
• Good for audio with excessive brightness or hiss
• Best for: Overly bright recordings, high-pitched noise

MODE 2 - TRAIN MODE (Seriously Degraded):
• Uses model in training mode for maximum restoration
• Most aggressive but may introduce artifacts
• Best for severely damaged audio quality
• Warning: Can distort very clean audio
• Best for: Heavily degraded, severely clipped, or very noisy audio

💡 START WITH MODE 0 - if unsatisfactory, try MODE 1 or 2

    Loads RVC (Real-time Voice Conversion) models trained on specific voices.
    These models learn the vocal characteristics of a target speaker.
    
    Key Features:
    • Supports .pth RVC model files
    • Optional FAISS index files for better similarity
    • Auto-download missing models
    • Model validation and caching
    
    Usage:
    • Connect output to narrator_target on Voice Changer node
    • Models should be placed in ComfyUI/models/RVC/ folder  
    • Index files should be in ComfyUI/models/RVC/.index/ folder
    
    Model Guide:
    • RVC models are speaker-specific (one model per voice)
    • Higher quality models require more training data
    • FAISS index improves voice similarity but increases processing time

TTS_engine.tooltip: Connect the RVC engine here because dataset prep also needs HuBERT and pitch-extraction settings, not just the later training node.

model_name.tooltip: Base name for the trained RVC voice. Changing only this should not force dataset re-prep when the actual data/settings stay the same.

dataset_source.tooltip: Optional folder, zip, or single audio file path. Relative paths resolve from ComfyUI input/ and input/datasets/. Clean single-speaker speech matters more than having one huge raw recording. Leave empty if you only use opt_audio inputs.

training_sample_rate.tooltip: Target training sample rate. 40k is the normal speech default and usually the right place to start.

cpu_workers.tooltip: CPU workers for slicing and feature extraction. 1-4 is usually enough; more is not automatically better, especially on Windows.

chunk_seconds.tooltip: Target clip length after slicing. RVC usually likes short clips; 3.0s is a good default, and an effective range around 2-8s is normal.

overlap_seconds.tooltip: Small overlap helps avoid harsh cuts between slices. Too much overlap just duplicates data and slows prep.

max_volume.tooltip: Peak normalization ceiling for extracted clips. 0.95 is a safe default; avoid pushing everything to 1.0 unless you like clipping risk.

mute_ratio.tooltip: Extra silence augmentation ratio. Leave this at 0 for normal training; raise it only if the model is over-voicing silence or breathing badly.

reuse_existing.tooltip: Reuse the prepared dataset cache when settings match. Usually keep this on; rebuilding features every run is just wasted time.

opt_audio1.tooltip: Optional training audio clip. Connect one or more AUDIO sources here for quick in-graph tests, or combine them with a dataset path.

epochs.tooltip: Actual RVC epoch count. Around 20 is a smoke test, 50-100 is a first real pass, and 100+ is where cleaner datasets usually become worth judging. Loss helps spot trends, but listening tests still decide quality.

batch_size.tooltip: Use the largest stable batch that fits VRAM. Bigger is usually faster and a bit smoother; lower it first if you hit OOM or instability.

learning_rate.tooltip: 1e-4 is the normal safe default. Lower it if training gets spiky or noisy; raising it is one of the fastest ways to make adversarial training worse.

gpu_ids.tooltip: CUDA device ids in the odd RVC format, for example '0' or '0-1'. Leave blank unless you deliberately want multi-GPU behavior.

num_workers.tooltip: PyTorch dataloader workers. Keep this at 0 on Windows; worker processes there can respawn ComfyUI internals and break training.

fp16_run.tooltip: Keep this on for normal CUDA training. Turn it off only if you see NaNs, weird instability, or hardware/driver-specific fp16 issues.

save_every_epoch.tooltip: Checkpoint cadence. Save a resumable training checkpoint every N epochs. 5 is a good default, 1 is safest, and 0 disables periodic resume checkpoints entirely.

cache_data_in_gpu.tooltip: Cache batches in VRAM for speed. Usually worth it if you have room; turn it off if VRAM pressure becomes the real bottleneck.

max_checkpoints.tooltip: Checkpoint retention policy. Keep the newest N checkpoint pairs and delete older ones. 1 means keep only the latest resumable checkpoint, 3 means keep the latest three, and so on.

save_every_weights.tooltip: Export extra standalone weight files at each save interval. Mostly useful for inspection or experiments; normal training does not need this.

train_index.tooltip: Build the matched FAISS index after training. Usually keep this on; normal RVC inference often sounds worse without the proper index.

save_best_model.tooltip: Track generator loss and save the lowest-loss model as an extra inference checkpoint candidate. Useful for listening tests, but lowest loss is not guaranteed to be the best sounding model.

best_model_threshold.tooltip: Initial gate for first 'best model' capture. Leave this alone unless you are debugging why low-loss checkpoint saving triggers too early or too often.

log_every_epoch.tooltip: Logging cadence within an epoch. This affects dashboard/log granularity, not training quality. 1.0 is about once per epoch, 0.5 is about twice.

pretrained_generator.tooltip: Generator initialization checkpoint. Keep this on auto unless you know exactly why you want a different base; training from scratch on a small dataset is usually a bad idea.

pretrained_discriminator.tooltip: Discriminator initialization checkpoint. Auto is the sane default and should stay matched to the generator/sample-rate setup.

c_adv.tooltip: Adversarial loss weight. Advanced knob. Do not touch this unless you are intentionally rebalancing training and understand the side effects.

c_mel.tooltip: Mel reconstruction weight. One of the main terms keeping speech recognizable. Usually leave it at default unless you are doing real loss tuning.

c_kl.tooltip: KL regularization weight. Changing this can absolutely destabilize training, so leave it alone unless you know the tradeoff you want.

c_fm.tooltip: Feature-matching weight. Usually helps texture/stability. Leave it at default unless you are deliberately rebalancing losses.

c_tefs.tooltip: Experimental TEFS auxiliary loss. Keep this at 0 unless you are explicitly experimenting with that feature.

c_hd.tooltip: Experimental harmonic-detail auxiliary loss. Keep this at 0 for normal training.

c_tsi.tooltip: Experimental TSI auxiliary loss. Keep this at 0 unless you are intentionally testing it.

c_gp.tooltip: Gradient-penalty weight. This is mostly a stabilization/debug knob, not a normal training control. Leave it at 0 unless adversarial loss is misbehaving.

use_multiscale.tooltip: Use experimental multiscale mel loss. Heavier and not needed for a normal first pass.

use_balancer.tooltip: Enable dynamic loss balancing. Advanced only. If you do not already know why you want this, you do not want this.

use_pareto.tooltip: Pareto-style balancing on top of the dynamic balancer. Ignore this unless you are already deliberately using the balancer.

fast_mode.tooltip: Speed tweak for the advanced balancer path. It does nothing useful unless you already enabled those advanced balancing options.

TTS_engine.tooltip: Connect a MOSS engine using a Delay 8B v1.0 or v1.5 model. Dataset preparation follows that selected base model.

model_name.tooltip: Base name for the trained MOSS LoRA adapter folder.

dataset_source.tooltip:
Path to a MOSS manifest JSONL or a folder of paired audio and transcript files.
For folders, use matching names such as clip001.wav + clip001.txt.
In the node workflow, connect the manifest path produced by MOSS Dataset Rows here.

validation_source.tooltip:
Optional second manifest JSONL used only for validation.

Use this if you already prepared a separate holdout set.
Example:
• dataset_source = your main training manifest
• validation_source = a smaller separate manifest reserved for evaluation

If you leave this blank, the node will automatically split dataset_source into train + validation for you.

validation_split.tooltip:
Only used when validation_source is blank.
Example: 0.05 means keep about 5% of dataset_source for validation and use the rest for training.

split_seed.tooltip: Seed for the automatic train/validation split, so the same manifest gets split the same way every time.

prep_batch_size.tooltip: Batch size for audio-code extraction during dataset prep.

n_vq.tooltip: Optional codec codebook count override. 0 uses the model default.

encode_reference_audio.tooltip:
Pre-encode reference audio fields during dataset prep.
Leave this on if your manifest uses ref_audio/reference_audio.
If you are doing normal audio+transcript training with no reference clips, this setting does not matter much.

reuse_existing.tooltip: Reuse a matching prepared dataset cache instead of re-encoding audio codes every run.

recursive_folder_scan.tooltip: When dataset_source or validation_source is a folder, also scan its subfolders. Disabled by default; direct files in the selected folder are always scanned.

training_mode.tooltip: Trains LoRA adapters for the selected MOSS Delay 8B v1.0 or v1.5 base model.

epochs.tooltip: Epoch count used when max_train_steps is 0.

max_train_steps.tooltip: Hard training-step cap. Set 0 to use epochs instead.

batch_size.tooltip: Per-device batch size. Keep it low on 8B models.

gradient_accumulation_steps.tooltip: Micro-batch accumulation. This is how you fake a larger effective batch without immediately OOMing.

learning_rate.tooltip: LoRA learning rate. The upstream Norwegian example used 2e-6.

warmup_steps.tooltip: Warmup step count before cosine decay.

max_grad_norm.tooltip: Gradient clipping. The upstream Norwegian example used 0.5.

num_workers.tooltip: Dataloader workers. 0 is the safest default.

gradient_checkpointing.tooltip: Keep this on for 8B training unless you deliberately want higher VRAM usage.

base_quantization.tooltip: Base-model VRAM strategy. 4bit_nf4 enables QLoRA-style loading of the frozen 8B base model with bitsandbytes. This is the main knob if 24 GB VRAM is still not enough.

bnb_4bit_compute_dtype.tooltip: Compute dtype used by 4-bit quantized layers. auto follows the mixed-precision choice. fp32 is safer but costs more VRAM.

bnb_4bit_use_double_quant.tooltip: Enable nested quantization for 4-bit base loading. Usually worth keeping on.

save_steps.tooltip: Checkpoint save cadence. 0 disables intermediate checkpoints.

trainable_lora_modules.tooltip: Which Delay backbone modules receive LoRA adapters. mlp matches the released Norwegian example best.

dataset_name.tooltip: Base name for the staged clip set. The output can feed engine-specific Dataset Rows nodes.

output_subdir.tooltip: Subdirectory inside ComfyUI input/ where reusable training clips will be written.

overwrite.tooltip: Overwrite the existing staged clip folder if it already exists.

opt_audio1.tooltip: Optional training audio clip. Connect one or more AUDIO sources here.

clip_dataset.tooltip: Staged clip dataset from Training Clip Staging.

manifest_name.tooltip: Output manifest filename. .jsonl will be appended if missing.

text_lines.default:
Hello there, this is a training sample.
How are you today?
text_lines.tooltip:
Exactly one line per staged clip, in clip order.
Each line is the transcription/text for that clip's target audio.
Simple training: just give each clip its own transcript here.
Example: clip001 audio says 'Hello there' -> line 1 should be 'Hello there'.

reference_clip_lines.tooltip:
Optional one line per staged clip.
Most single-speaker or fixed-voice LoRAs should leave this blank.
Use this only if a training row should also include reference audio for voice/style conditioning.
That means: text says what to say, target clip is the correct output, and reference clip says whose voice/style to follow.
Leave blank for normal audio+transcript training.
Each line may be blank, a single clip id like clip001, a 1-based clip number like 1, or a comma-separated list such as clip001,clip002.
Example: line 2 = clip001 means clip002 trains as: text from line 2 + reference voice from clip001 -> target audio clip002.
Single reference -> ref_audio. Multiple references -> reference_audio.

language_lines.tooltip: Optional one line per clip. Blank line uses default_language or no language field.

instruction_lines.tooltip:
Optional one line per clip. Blank line uses default_instruction.
Use this for explicit labels such as 'speaking angrily', 'whispering', or 'calm narration'.
Do not use this for recording/presentation labels like 'telephone call quality'; those belong in quality_lines.
For many style-focused datasets, this is easier and clearer than using reference_clip_lines.

quality_lines.tooltip:
Optional one line per clip. Blank line uses default_quality.
Use this for recording/presentation labels such as 'telephone call quality', 'studio recording', or similar audio-quality descriptors.

sound_event_lines.tooltip: Optional one line per clip. Blank line uses default_sound_event.

ambient_sound_lines.tooltip: Optional one line per clip. Blank line uses default_ambient_sound.

duration_tokens_lines.tooltip: Optional one line per clip. Blank line uses default_duration_tokens.

default_language.tooltip: Optional shared language fallback for rows whose language_lines entry is blank.

default_instruction.tooltip:
Optional shared instruction fallback for rows whose instruction_lines entry is blank.
Useful if most rows should carry the same style label, for example 'speaking angrily'.

default_quality.tooltip:
Optional shared quality fallback.
Useful if most rows share the same recording/presentation quality label, for example 'telephone call quality'.

default_duration_tokens.tooltip: Optional shared tokens fallback. 0 disables it.

output_subdir.tooltip: Subdirectory inside ComfyUI input/ where the generated manifest file will be written.

overwrite.tooltip: Overwrite the existing manifest file if it already exists.

TTS_engine.tooltip: Connect a DramaBox engine. Its selected model supplies the official transformer, audio components, and Gemma paths.

model_name.tooltip: Name used for the prepared dataset and eventual managed LoRA adapter.

dataset_source.tooltip: JSONL/JSON manifest, TSV, gemini_synthetic index, or libriheavy index. Manifest rows should contain audio_filepath/audio_path and text/transcript.

dataset_type.tooltip: Input format. The suite converts every format into the official ~-delimited speaker index used by the trainer.

audio_dir.tooltip: Base folder for relative audio paths. Blank resolves paths relative to the dataset file.

min_duration.tooltip: Minimum clip duration passed to the official preprocessor.

max_duration.tooltip: Maximum clip duration passed to the official preprocessor.

reuse_existing.tooltip: Reuse a matching normalized index and already-preprocessed cache when available.

preprocess_now.tooltip: Run the official Gemma/audio-VAE preprocessing now. Turn this off to prepare only the CPU-side index and let Model Training preprocess later.

dry_run.tooltip: CPU-safe index-only mode. No model download, Gemma load, or CUDA preprocessing is started.

clip_dataset.tooltip: Staged audio from Training Clip Staging.

manifest_name.tooltip: Output manifest filename. .jsonl is appended when missing.

transcript_lines.default:
Hello there, this is a training sample.
This is the second sample from the same speaker.
transcript_lines.tooltip: Exactly one line per staged clip, in clip order. Blank lines skip the corresponding clip.

speaker_lines.tooltip: Optional speaker name per clip. Blank lines use default_speaker.

language_lines.tooltip: Optional language code per clip. Blank lines use default_language.

default_speaker.tooltip: Speaker assigned when the corresponding speaker line is blank. Each DramaBox speaker needs at least two clips.

default_language.tooltip: Language code assigned when the corresponding language line is blank.

output_subdir.tooltip: Subdirectory inside ComfyUI input/ for the generated manifest.

overwrite.tooltip: Overwrite an existing manifest with the same name.

training_mode.tooltip: Official DramaBox audio-branch IC-LoRA training mode.

base_model.tooltip: Official timestep schedule. dev is the normal DramaBox fine-tuning choice; distilled is experimental.

steps.tooltip: Optimizer steps. The upstream example uses 10,000; listen to saved checkpoints instead of assuming the final step is best.

learning_rate.tooltip: LoRA learning rate. The official example uses 1e-4 for a fresh adapter.

batch_size.tooltip: Per-device batch size. Keep this at 1 unless the dataset and GPU have room.

grad_accum.tooltip: Gradient accumulation steps. This increases effective batch size without loading more samples at once.

lora_rank.tooltip: LoRA rank. The official DramaBox example uses 128.

lora_alpha.tooltip: LoRA alpha. Keeping alpha equal to rank gives a 1.0 adapter scale.

lora_dropout.tooltip: LoRA dropout. The official small-dataset example uses 0.1.

lr_scheduler.tooltip: Learning-rate schedule passed to the official trainer.

warmup_steps.tooltip: Warmup steps before the selected schedule. The official example uses 500.

ref_ratio.tooltip: Fraction of a training target used as the appended voice-reference tail.

max_ref_tokens.tooltip: Maximum reference tokens after audio patchification.

text_dropout.tooltip: Probability of dropping text conditioning so the adapter learns to use the reference voice path.

save_every.tooltip: Checkpoint cadence. The official trainer requires a value of at least 1.

log_every.tooltip: Human-readable console update cadence. The training panel receives quieter per-step updates.

seed.tooltip: Training random seed.

preprocess_batch_size.tooltip: Audio/text preprocessing batch size. Lower this if preprocessing runs out of memory.

validation_config.tooltip: Optional path to the official val_config YAML. Validation launches another full inference process at each save step and requires a separate GPU.

validation_gpu.tooltip: Physical CUDA device index reserved for validation, for example 1. Required when validation_config is set and must differ from the training GPU.

dry_run.tooltip: CPU-safe preflight only: writes the normalized official config and command without loading DramaBox weights or starting CUDA training.

text.default:
Enter your text here. Examples:
Polish: Cześć, jak się masz?
German: Schöne Grüße aus München!
French: Bonjour, comment allez-vous?
text.tooltip:
Input text to normalize for TTS processing.

Supports multilingual text with special characters like:
• Polish: ą, ć, ę, ł, ń, ó, ś, ź, ż
• German: ä, ö, ü, ß
• French: à, é, ê, ç, etc.
• And many other languages

Connect this to any TTS engine for improved pronunciation.

method.tooltip:
Text processing method to apply:

• Pass-through: No processing (original text)
• Unicode Decomposition: ą→a̧, ć→ć (recommended for most cases)
• IPA Phonemization: Full phonetic conversion (ą→ɔ̃, requires espeak)
• Character Mapping: ASCII fallback (ą→a, ć→c)

Start with Unicode Decomposition - it fixes most pronunciation issues.

language.tooltip:
Language for processing (affects IPA Phonemization):

• Auto-detect: Automatically detects language from text
• Manual selection: Choose specific language for better accuracy

Language detection looks for special characters:
• Polish: ą, ę, ć, ł, etc.
• German: ä, ö, ü, ß
• French: à, é, ê, ç, etc.

Only affects IPA Phonemization method.

show_debug.tooltip:
Show debug information in console:

• Original vs normalized text comparison
• Character-by-character changes
• Detected language (when auto-detecting)
• Processing method used

Helpful for testing which method works best for your language.
Disable for cleaner console output in production.

text.default: this was designed mainly for raw asr outputs like granite but it can clean up any plain text transcript as well
text.tooltip:
Raw text to post-process with punctuation and true-casing.

Designed mainly for low-punctuation ASR outputs such as Granite transcripts, but it can be used on any plain text transcript.

Important: this expects plain transcript text, not full SRT files with cue numbers and timestamps.

Best results usually come from lowercased, lightly cleaned ASR text rather than already-punctuated prose.
If a paragraph already looks properly punctuated, the node now skips repunctuating that paragraph automatically instead of making it worse.

model.tooltip:
Choose the punctuation/truecase model.

English is the lightest option.
Romance covers ES/FR/IT/PT/CA/GL.
XLM-R is the heavy multilingual fallback.

These are helper models, not ASR engines.

processing_scope.tooltip:
How to feed text to the punctuation model.

Whole Text: process the entire input as one block.
Per Paragraph: split on blank lines first and preserve paragraph breaks.

output_mode.tooltip:
How to format the output text.

Restored Paragraphs: normal punctuated text.
One Sentence Per Line: useful for subtitle prep, manual review, or later segmentation.

lowercase_input_first.tooltip:
Lowercase the input before running the punctuation model.

Recommended for raw ASR text because these helper models are mainly trained for lowercased, unpunctuated transcripts.
Disable only if you are intentionally experimenting with already-cased input.

signal.tooltip: Primary signal input. Connect this to the output of a node that creates new voice files (e.g., Voice Designer) to ensure voices are refreshed after file creation.

signal2.tooltip: Secondary passthrough signal. Use this to chain execution order: connect your ENGINE/config here, and connect signal2_out to downstream TTS nodes. This ensures TTS nodes run after voice cache refresh.

force_refresh.tooltip: Force a full rescan of voice folders and alias map.

provider.tooltip:
Computer vision provider for mouth movement detection:

• MediaPipe: Google's ML framework (preferred, incompatible with Python 3.13)
  - Fast, accurate, works on most hardware
  - Best for general use and consistent results

• OpenSeeFace: Real-time face tracking (experimental, Python 3.13 compatible)
  - Alternative for newer Python versions
  - Results may be less accurate than MediaPipe

• dlib: Traditional computer vision (coming soon)
  - Lightweight, no ML dependencies

sensitivity.tooltip:
Ultra-fine movement detection sensitivity (exponential scaling):

• 0.05-0.2: Only obvious mouth movements (conservative)
• 0.3-0.4: Clear speech detection (balanced)
• 0.5-0.6: Most speech including soft talking
• 0.7-0.8: Sensitive, catches subtle movements
• 0.9-1.0: Ultra-sensitive, includes whispers and micro-movements

Exponential scaling provides fine control at higher values.
Start with 0.5, then fine-tune in 0.01 increments.

min_duration.tooltip:
Minimum duration for valid speech segments (in seconds):

Lower values: Include quick sounds and short words, more segments
Higher values: Only longer phrases, cleaner but may miss short words

Recommended: 0.1s for balanced filtering, 0.05s for detailed analysis

output_format.tooltip:
Output format for timing data:

• SRT: Standard subtitle format, best for TTS synchronization
• JSON: Detailed data with confidence scores for analysis
• CSV: Spreadsheet format for data processing
• AUDIO_REGIONS: start,end format compatible with Audio Analyzer

Recommended: SRT for TTS workflows, AUDIO_REGIONS for audio analysis

srt_placeholder_format.tooltip:
SRT placeholder format - adapts to viseme detection:

🔌 WITHOUT Viseme Options:
• Words: [word word word] - estimated word placeholders
• Syllables: [syl-la-ble syl-la-ble] - estimated syllable patterns
• Characters: [••••••••••••••••••••] - character count

🔗 WITH Viseme Options connected:
• Words: [A EI OU] - vowels grouped as words
• Syllables: [AE-I-OU] - vowels grouped as syllables
• Characters: [AEIOU] - raw vowel sequence

Format = presentation style, visemes = actual vowel content!

viseme_options.tooltip:
Connect Viseme Mouth Shape Options node for vowel detection (A, E, I, O, U):

• When connected: Enables precise vowel classification
• When not connected: Basic speech/no-speech detection only

Viseme detection adds ~20% processing time but provides detailed mouth shape analysis for lip-sync.

preview_mode.label: Show preview with movement markers
preview_mode.tooltip:
Generate annotated video preview with movement markers:

Shows green/red overlays for detected/undetected movements with confidence scores and facial landmarks.

Performance: Uses 540p resolution, increases processing time by ~40%

Use for: Debugging detection accuracy and tuning parameters

clean_subtitle_output.label: Clean Subtitle Output
clean_subtitle_output.tooltip:
Remove all brackets, confidence scores, and metadata from output:

• OFF: [hello world] (confidence: 74.2%, 1.1s)
• ON: hello world

Use when you want clean subtitles ready for direct use without technical information.

merge_threshold.label: Merge gaps shorter than (seconds)
merge_threshold.tooltip:
Merge nearby speech segments separated by short gaps:

Lower values: Keep more segments separate, preserve natural pauses
Higher values: Merge more segments together, smoother but less detailed

Recommended: 0.2s for natural flow, 1.0s+ for sentence-level segments

confidence_threshold.tooltip:
Minimum confidence score for including detected movements:

• 0.0-0.2: Include all detections (may include noise)
• 0.3-0.4: Balanced filtering (recommended start)
• 0.5-0.7: Conservative, only clear movements
• 0.8-1.0: Ultra-strict, only highest confidence

Confidence based on landmark quality, face visibility, lighting.
With new exponential sensitivity, lower values work better.

enable_viseme_detection.label: Enable Viseme Detection
enable_viseme_detection.tooltip:
Enable vowel classification (A, E, I, O, U) for precise lip-sync:

• Analyzes mouth shape geometry beyond simple open/close
• Detects vowel patterns in mouth movements
• Adds ~20% processing time
• Provides phoneme sequences for better TTS synchronization

viseme_sensitivity.tooltip:
How hard should I look for vowels?

Controls geometric thresholds for mouth shape classification:

• 0.1-0.5: Very strict, only obvious vowel shapes
• 0.8-1.2: Balanced detection (recommended)
• 1.5-2.0: Lenient, detects subtle vowel variations

Higher = more detections, may include false positives
Lower = fewer detections, higher accuracy

viseme_confidence_threshold.tooltip:
How sure should I be before showing a vowel?

Minimum confidence for valid viseme classification:

• 0.0-0.2: Show all viseme attempts (noisy)
• 0.3-0.5: Balanced filtering (recommended)
• 0.6-0.8: Conservative, only clear vowels
• 0.9-1.0: Ultra-strict, only perfect detections

Below threshold shows as 'neutral' instead of uncertain vowel.

viseme_smoothing.tooltip:
Temporal smoothing to reduce viseme flickering:

• 0.0: No smoothing (immediate response, may flicker)
• 0.3: Light smoothing (recommended balance)
• 0.7: Heavy smoothing (stable but slower response)
• 1.0: Maximum smoothing (very stable, delayed)

Reduces rapid switching between visemes for cleaner sequences.
Useful for noisy videos or subtle mouth movements.

enable_consonant_detection.label: Enable Consonant Detection
enable_consonant_detection.tooltip:
Detect consonants (B, P, M, F, V, TH, etc.) in addition to vowels:

• Vowels only: A, E, I, O, U, _
• With consonants: A, E, I, O, U, B, P, M, F, V, TH, _, etc.
• Adds ~10% processing time
• Provides more detailed phoneme sequences
• Better for advanced lip-sync and speech analysis

Leave disabled for basic vowel-only detection.

enable_temporal_analysis.label: Enable Temporal Analysis
enable_temporal_analysis.tooltip:
Advanced consonant burst detection using 5-frame windows:

• Analyzes onset → peak → release patterns for true consonants
• Dramatically improves B/P/M distinction accuracy
• Detects rapid lip closure/release vs sustained patterns
• Better coarticulation modeling (vowel context)
• Adds ~50% processing time but much higher accuracy
• Requires consonant detection enabled

Recommended for: research, high-quality phonetic analysis
Skip for: basic lip-sync, real-time processing

enable_word_prediction.label: Enable Word Prediction
enable_word_prediction.tooltip:
Predict words from detected phoneme sequences:

• Uses 10,000 most common English words
• Matches phoneme patterns to suggest likely words
• Shows confidence with ?, (), markers
• Example: 'AEIOU' → 'you', 'hey?', '(audio)'
• Helpful for manual SRT editing
• No processing time impact

Requires viseme detection enabled to work.

voice_to_clone.tooltip: Optional: Reference voice to clone. If not provided, synthetic voice will be used.

temperature.tooltip: Only used when sampling is enabled

top_p.tooltip: Only used when sampling is enabled

max_words_per_chunk.tooltip: Maximum words per chunk for long texts. Lower values prevent speed issues but create more chunks.

voice_speed_factor.tooltip: 1.0 = normal speed, <1.0 = slower speed, >1.0 = faster speed

attention_type.tooltip: Attention implementation. Auto selects the best available, eager is standard, sdpa is optimized PyTorch, flash_attention_2 requires compatible GPU, sage uses quantized attention for speedup (CUDA only)

randomize_subject_in_directory.tooltip: ON: each queue picks a random subject .txt from the same folder as the selected subject (SubjectFiles subfolder). Live subject pane is ignored while this is on. OFF: always use the selected subject.

model_low.tooltip: Optional second MODEL branch (Wan low-noise, or MiniMax R2V UNET). Passed through even without clip_low — Low LoRA slots still apply to this model (clip_high is used only as the LoRA companion).

clip_low.tooltip: Optional second CLIP for dual high/low stacks. Omit for single-CLIP graphs (e.g. MiniMax); model_low still passes through.

prepend_text.tooltip: Optional: wired prepend for main prompt and for prompt_override (scenario [Prompt] or [description]/[desciption]).

post_text.tooltip: Optional: wired post text after the subject block on main prompt, and before scenario [Prompt] body on prompt_override.

global_selector_input.tooltip: From Lazy Global Selector. Used as [Workflow] in the selector blob when subject/scenario files do not set [Workflow].

subject_live.tooltip: Synced by live editor extension (not shown on node).

seed.tooltip: LLM seed. -1 = random each run.

lm_studio_model.placeholder: Model id as shown in LM Studio

lm_studio_ttl.tooltip: LM Studio JIT unload: when > 0, unloads the model immediately after each run via /api/v1/models/unload (v1 chat). On OpenAI fallback only, also sends idle TTL in the request body. 0 = leave loaded.

max_output_tokens.tooltip: Hard cap on completion length (HF max_new_tokens / LM Studio max_tokens / TextGenerate max_length). The pacing hint asks the model for ~one-third of this many tokens by default — raise both together for longer prompts (e.g. 1500 max → ~500 target).

system_prompt.placeholder: Leave empty = Model_Skills template for target_model
system_prompt.tooltip: Optional full system override. Empty = selected skill's Model_Skills/*.md prompt. Does not merge with the MD body. textgenerate_thinking.tooltip: TextGenerate (CLIP) only: enable thinking mode when the wired LLM supports it.
